w:r.w:t: SENTINEL
Pre-Release Master Checklist
VS Code Extension • GitHub Repository • CLI Companion
Complete every checkbox before public release. Critical items marked in red.
How to use this checklist

Work through each section in order. Every ☐ must be ticked before moving to the next phase. Items marked [CRITICAL] are hard blockers — the extension cannot ship without them. All other items are required but can be completed in any order within their section. When every checkbox in every section is ticked, Sentinel is ready for public release.

PART D — DETECTION ENGINE
D1 — Contradiction Detection
[CRITICAL]
Contradiction detector runs on every file save
Detects: inconsistent function usage across files
Detects: data-shape drift — same data structured differently in different files
Detects: duplicate solutions — same problem solved two different ways
Detects: async/callback mismatch — one pattern used in some files, other in others
Detects: function signature conflicts — defined one way, called differently
Severity Info: logged silently to vault, not shown in UI unless user checks vault
Severity Warning: sidebar alert panel entry created
Severity Critical: always surfaces — badge in sidebar even in passive mode
Each contradiction logged to vault with: file, line reference, description, severity, timestamp
Contradiction alert includes: what contradicts, where the original decision was made, suggested fix
D2 — Contradiction Resolution
Manual resolve: user clicks Mark as Resolved in sidebar — logged with timestamp
Auto-resolve: Sentinel detects offending code changed on file save
Auto-resolve checks BOTH current file AND all related files flagged in same contradiction
If current file fixed but related files still show old pattern: stays open, alert updated to 'partially addressed'
Project override: user adds entry to overrides.yml — contradiction marked as intentional exception
Resolved contradictions removed from active alerts but kept in vault history
Unresolved contradictions carried forward to every future session report
D3 — Bad Practice Detection
[CRITICAL]
Bad practice scanner runs on every file save
Detects: god functions — single function with too many responsibilities
Detects: deep nesting — 3 or more levels of nested logic
Detects: mixed concerns — multiple unrelated responsibilities in one file
Detects: hardcoded secrets — API keys, passwords, tokens in source code
Detects: undefined variables used in code
Detects: missing or phantom imports — imported packages not installed
Detects: naming inconsistency — different conventions across files
Each finding logged to vault with file, line reference, type, severity, timestamp
Findings shown in sidebar Session panel as feed items
